rich_summary: Parasurama, the formidable Brahmin-warrior who once exterminated the Kshatriya class to avenge his father Jamadagni, confronts Rama after hearing of the breaking of Shiva’s bow. He presents the bow of Vishnu—its divine counterpart—and challenges Rama to string it. Rama calmly accepts. With controlled anger he effortlessly seizes the bow, strings it, and sets a divine arrow that cannot be withdrawn without fulfilling its purpose. The act shakes the three worlds and draws the gods to witness the moment. Realizing Rama’s true nature, Parasurama recognizes him as Vishnu incarnate and submits. Rather than kill the sage, Rama strips him of the glory and power gained through austerities, forcing him to withdraw to Mount Mahendra. The episode marks the symbolic transfer of divine warrior authority from the old avataric hero to Rama.

highlight_spans.why: Introduction of Vishnu’s divine bow, establishing the mythic weapon whose mastery will reveal Rama’s true stature.
Rama boldly seizes the bow from Parasurama and strings it, the decisive action proving his superiority.
Rama declares the divine arrow cannot return to the quiver without accomplishing its purpose, raising the stakes of the confrontation.
Cosmic reaction: the three worlds tremble and the gods assemble, underscoring the divine scale of the moment.
Parasurama’s humbled recognition that Rama is Vishnu Himself and his acceptance of defeat.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama calmly draws the colossal bow of Vishnu and sets a blazing divine arrow while Parasurama stands stunned before him.
As Rama fully draws the bow, the heavens fill with gods, gandharvas, and apsaras watching while the three worlds tremble.
The once‑fearsome Parasurama, stripped of his power, bows humbly before the radiant Rama and acknowledges him as Vishnu incarnate.
